answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, limiting influence to identities reachable from trusted roots. A hollow sybil cluster with few honest links has low conductance, so little walk probability escapes it; min-cut bounds therefore constrain the trust mass entering from outside. If votes are capped by that walk-derived mass, even a lotus of colluding identities at the conductance nadir cannot amplify its aggregate voting weight merely by adding identities.
